record.file_problem: Repository text contains metadata, the README, and only the first 400 entries of the file list; code and experiment records were not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The README describes using a refusal-direction write as part of a known-unknown abstention method and reports that method's performance. It does not test the claim's refusal behavior on harmful or harmless requests.
record.gate_note: The README reports direction-write results for abstention on unknown questions, not refusal rates for harmful or harmless user requests. Its statements about other model families do not identify the models or give a result tied to the claim versions.
record.test_reason: The README uses an orthogonalized refusal-direction write as a tool. A known-unknown probe gates the write to turn confabulations on unanswerable questions into abstentions, and only that method's performance is reported (conversion rate, known-correct cost, depth, controls). No refusal rates are given on harmful or harmless requests. There is no ablation, no test of how the direction was derived (difference-in-means or otherwise), and no capability check.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that internal signals cannot make the model use its own answerability signal, but that an external loop works. In that loop, a known-unknown probe gates an orthogonalized refusal-direction write, which converts most held-out confabulations to abstentions at low cost on Qwen3-4B, passes fake-part controls, and depends on write depth. They add that direction-specificity is family-dependent.
record.recipe_differences: A research-workspace repository, not a replication of the original refusal-direction method. The README describes a gated, orthogonalized direction write for known-unknown abstention, rather than the claimed difference-in-means direction removal/addition tests.
record.method_sensitivity: The README says write depth changes the reported abstention conversion (89.2% at a calibrated mid-band site versus 66.5% late) and that direction-specificity holds in some model families and fails in others, without identifying those families.

fits_no_version.finding: A known-unknown probe gating an orthogonalized refusal-direction write converts 73.5% of held-out confabulations to abstentions at 3.1% known-correct cost on Qwen3-4B. Conversion is 89.2% at a calibrated mid-band layer versus 66.5% late. Fake-part controls collapse the effect.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A refusal direction, written conditionally on a known-unknown probe, can induce abstention on unanswerable questions; the effect depends on write depth and on model family.

record.problems: The README is a repository overview, not the underlying experiment reports; the reported outcomes lack uncertainty estimates and detailed conditions here. The file list is truncated and the code and experiment records were not read or run.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant outcomes are reported in the supplied README. The README's statement about direction-specificity across some model families lacks named subjects and specific outcomes, so it was not extracted as a model-level row.

untested.parts: Ablation removing refusal, addition inducing refusal on harmless requests, and capability retention are all untested. The write induces abstention on unknown questions only, through a probe gate.
No jailbreak analysis or adversarial training.
No multi-direction, affine or cone analysis.
The README says 'direction-specificity holds in some families and fails in others', but the families are unnamed, no numbers are given, and the finding concerns the abstention effect.
No training-dependence test of the refusal direction. The SFT/DPO/KTO/GRPO training targets abstention, not refusal-direction existence.

missing.what: How the refusal direction was derived (e.g. difference-in-means on harmful/harmless prompts) and whether its ungated effect on harmful or harmless refusal was measured. If so, this could bear on V1 induction. It is not in the README.
Per-family results on direction-specificity (which families hold and which fail).

record.verdict_notes: Only the README was available; the manuscripts and experiment records were not. The README contains instructions addressed to reviewing agents (e.g. to traverse the repository and audit it); these were ignored. The refusal direction is borrowed as an actuator, which places the study at T4. Even if the Paper 5 manuscript contains ungated refusal-induction results, the README gives none.

versions.untested_parts: No harmful-request refusal removal or harmless-request refusal induction is reported; no test of retained general capabilities.
No weight edit or released-model abliteration result is reported.
No jailbreak suppression of the direction or training against its ablation is reported.
No test of affine, cone, or multiple-direction accounts of refusal is reported.
No separation of harmfulness judgment from refusal decision is tested.
No identified cross-language, base-to-instruct, or model-variant transfer test of the claimed refusal direction is reported.
No test of how refusal-training choices affect existence of a removable direction is reported.
